title: Hildred Carlile

{{Short description|British politician (1852–1942)}} [[File:Hildred Carlile, Vanity Fair, 1909-12-23.jpg|thumb|"[[:en:St Albans (UK Parliament constituency)|Mid Herts]]", caricature by [[Luke Fildes|Elf]] in [[Vanity Fair (UK)|Vanity Fair]], 1909.]] {{EngvarB|date=October 2013}} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2024}} '''Sir Edward Hildred Carlile, 1st Baronet''', {{post nominals|GBR|CBE}} (10 July 1852 – 26 September 1942) was an English businessman and [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] politician. == Early life == Born in [[Richmond, London|Richmond]], Surrey, in 1852, Carlile was educated at [[St Albans School (Hertfordshire)|St Albans School]] and abroad. He made his career in business and politics. In business he was a partner in the firm of Jonas Brook & Brothers, [[Meltham#Meltham Mills|Meltham Mills]], [[Huddersfield]]. This firm later merged with J. & P. Coats Limited (now [[Coats plc]]), and he became a Director of that company. == Politics == He stood unsuccessfully in [[Huddersfield (UK Parliament constituency)|Huddersfield]] at the [[1900 United Kingdom general election|1900 general election]].{{cite book |last=Craig |first=F. W. S. |author-link= F. W. S. Craig |title=British parliamentary election results 1885–1918 |orig-year=1974 |edition= 2nd |year=1989 |publisher= Parliamentary Research Services |location=Chichester |isbn= 0-900178-27-2 |page=122 }} He was elected as the [[Member of Parliament#United Kingdom|Member of Parliament]] (MP) for [[St Albans (UK Parliament constituency)|St Albans]] at the [[1906 United Kingdom general election|1906 general election]].Craig, ''British parliamentary election results 1885–1918'', page 297 He was re-elected at both the elections in 1910, and returned unopposed as a [[Coalition Conservative]] in [[1918 United Kingdom general election|1918]].{{cite book |last=Craig |first=F. W. S. |author-link= F. W. S. Craig |title=British parliamentary election results 1918–1949 |orig-year=1969 |edition=3rd |year=1983 |publisher= Parliamentary Research Services |location=Chichester |isbn= 0-900178-06-X |page=375 }} Due to ill-healthBy-election at St Albans: Sir E.H. Carlile to retire through ill-health, ''The Times'', 21 November 1919, page 9 he [[resignation from the British House of Commons|resigned]] from the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] on 20 November 1919 by the procedural device of accepting appointment as [[Steward of the Manor of Northstead]].{{cite web |url=http://www.parliament.uk/documents/commons/lib/research/briefings/snpc-04731.pdf |title=Appointments to the Chiltern Hundreds and Manor of Northstead Stewardships since 1850 |author=Department of Information Services |publisher=[[House of Commons Library]] |date=14 January 2010 |access-date=13 August 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110206041753/http://www.parliament.uk/documents/commons/lib/research/briefings/snpc-04731.pdf |archive-date=6 February 2011 }} He was a [[Justice of the Peace|J.P.]] for [[Hertfordshire]], the [[West Riding of Yorkshire]], and for the [[County borough|Borough]] of Huddersfield. From 1910 to 1919 he was a member of the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] Accounts Committee. He was also active in the [[Yeomanry]] and [[Volunteer Force|Volunteers]], eventually becoming Honorary Colonel of the [[Huddersfield Rifles|5th Battalion Duke of Wellington's Regiment]] (1906–39).''Army Lists''. During [[World War I]] he worked for the [[Red Cross]]. He unsuccessfully stood as the Conservative candidate in the [[1921 Hertford by-election]] == Philanthropy == In 1914 he gave 100,000 [[Guinea (British coin)|guinea]]s (an enormous sum in those days) as an endowment to [[Bedford College (London)|Bedford College, University of London]] (he was the first Fellow on the Council of the College), which made possible the establishment of Chairs in Botany, English, Latin, and Physics.[http://www.british-history.ac.uk/report.asp?compid=22145 The University of London – The Constituent Colleges | British History Online] at www.british-history.ac.uk He was [[Knight bachelor|knighted]] in 1911,{{London Gazette |issue=28512 |date=11 July 1911 |page=5167}} appointed [[deputy lieutenant]] of [[Hertfordshire]] in 1912,{{London Gazette | issue=28620 |page=4469 | date=21 June 1912}} created a [[baronet]], of Ponsbourne Park, in the [[County of Hertford]] on 27 June 1917,{{London Gazette |issue=30255 |date=28 August 1917 |page=8891}} and appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in 1920.{{London Gazette |issue=31840 |date=30 March 1920 |page=3762 |supp=y}} In 1922 he was [[High Sheriff of Hertfordshire]].{{London Gazette |issue=32642 |date=17 March 1922 |page=2231}} One of his brothers was [[Wilson Carlile]], founder of the [[Church Army]], of which Hildred was a vice-president. At age 90 he died, like his latter brother, in 1942. == References == {{Reflist}} *Entry in ''[[Who's Who (UK)|Who's Who]]'' *Records, [[Royal Holloway, University of London]] *[http://rcnarchive.rcn.org.uk/data/VOLUME052-1914/page061-volume52-24thjanuary1914.pdf ''British Journal of Nursing'', January 24, 1914] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20061101082804/http://www.colonialcdbooks.com/carlile.htm Carlile family genealogy] == External links == * {{Hansard-contribs | sir-edward-carlile | Hildred Carlile }} {{S-start}} {{s-par|uk}} {{succession box | title = [[Member of Parliament]] for [[St Albans (UK Parliament constituency)|St Albans]] | years = [[1906 United Kingdom general election|1906]]–[[1919 St Albans by-election|1919]] | before = [[John Bamford Slack]] | after = [[Francis Edward Fremantle|Sir Francis Edward Fremantle]] }} {{s-hon}} {{s-bef | before=[[Arthur Cory-Wright|Sir Arthur Cory-Wright]]}} {{s-ttl | title=[[High Sheriff of Hertfordshire]] | years=1922}} {{s-aft | after=George Strachan Pawle}} {{s-reg|uk-bt}} {{s-new | creation}} {{s-ttl | title=[[Carlile baronets|Baronet]]
